proposition: Grammatology and New Brethren call Ibn Turka Shāfiʿī chief judge of Isfahan and Yazd, and New Brethren says he inherited both. The dissertation has the Isfahan qadiship as a family office descended from Ṣadr al-Dīn's appointment at Samarkand, and has the Yazd judgeship granted by Shāhrukh c. 825/1422 at Ibn Turka's own request after his first Herat proceeding.

mediation.who: Ibn Turka, Nafsat al-Maṣdūr I/II, as reported by Melvin-Koushki
mediation.note: written to the rulers judging him; the dissertation calls the apologies the primary source for his life (pdf 75)

mediation.who: Melvin-Koushki, The New Brethren of Purity
